definition.title: Appreciating your experience with Vertix
definition.description:
We want to thank you for your time and patience.

**Your experience with Vertix is important to us, and we would love to hear your feedback.**

We strive to provide the best possible service, and your input can help us achieve that.

If you have any suggestions, concerns, or ideas on how we can improve Vertix, please don't hesitate to share them with us.

Your feedback is highly appreciated and will contribute to making Vertix even better.

Thank you for using Vertix, and we look forward to hearing your thoughts!

definition.title: 🛠  Setup Vertix
definition.description:
Discover the limitless possibilities of **Vertix**!
Customize and optimize your server to perfection.

To create a new master channel just click:
`(➕ Create Master Channel)` button.

Master Channels are dynamic voice channel generators, each with its own unique configuration.

Our badwords feature enables guild-level configuration for limiting dynamic channel names.

_**Current master channels**_:
{masterChannelMessage}

_**Server Badwords**_:
{badwordsMessage}

_**Server Voice Role**_:
{voiceRoleMessage}

_**Server Verified Roles**_:
{verifiedRolesMessage}

_**Server Staff Roles**_:
{staffRolesMessage}

-# 💡 You can set logs channel by editing the master channel.

definition.title: 🤷  You have reached your master channels limit
definition.description: You can create up to **{maxMasterChannels}** Master Channels in total.

definition.title: ⏱️  Claim Configuration
➕  Create a channel generator
definition.description:
A generator is a voice channel members join to get one of their own, made for them and removed when they leave.

**✨ Dynamic Channel (V3)** — the current interface. Pick this unless you have a reason not to.
**➕ Dynamic Channel (V2)** — the older interface, for servers already running it.
**📈 Auto-Scaling Channel** — one channel that grows into several as it fills up.

Choose below, and the rest is a few questions.

definition.title: 🔧  Edit a channel generator
definition.description:
Pick the generator you want to change.

Its settings open next — the name new channels get, who may see them, which buttons their owners have, and the rest.

*Nothing here? The server has no generators yet — `/manage new-generator` makes one.*

definition.title: ⚙️  Server settings
definition.description:
Settings that belong to the whole server rather than to one generator.

**Voice Role** — given to members while they are in a voice channel.
**Verified Roles** — who dynamic channels are for.
**Staff Roles** — who may act on a channel they do not own.
**Bad Words** — words a member cannot put in a channel name.
**Claim** — how long an abandoned channel waits, and how long the vote runs.

Pick one to change it.

definition.title: 🛡️  Server roles
definition.description:
Which roles this server's dynamic channels answer to.

**Voice Role** — given to members while they are in a voice channel, and taken back when they leave.
**Verified Roles** — who the channels are for. Everyone else is kept out.
**Staff Roles** — who may act on a channel they do not own.

Pick one to change it.

definition.title: 🙅  Bad Words
definition.description:
Words that cannot appear in the name of a dynamic channel, anywhere in this server.

A member renaming their channel to something holding one of these is told no and the name is left as it was. The check is on names only - it does not read what anyone says.

_**Current list**_:
{badwordsMessage}

`(🙅 Edit Bad Words)` replaces the whole list with what you type, separated by commas.
`(🧹 Remove all)` empties it, which allows every name again.

definition.title: ༄ Vertix is here, let's get started!
definition.description:
Welcome to Vertix, an incredible addition to your server!
Let's collaborate and make your server even better.

**Bot Setup**
- Type `/setup` or press `(🛠 Setup)` button.
- Click on `(➕ Create Master Channel)`
- Follow the steps.

Still not sure? Check out our [step by step](https://voicechannels.online/posts/how-to-setup) guide.

You can always edit the configurations by using the `/setup` command.

If you need assistance or have any suggestions, feel free to join our Discord community server! We would be glad to help you and hear your feedback.

Join us at: https://discord.gg/dEwKeQefUU

rateLimited.{rateLimitedDisplay}:
⚠️ Renaming cannot be performed at the moment due to rate limit restrictions.

Please wait for {elapsedTimeFormatFraction} seconds or create a new channel instead.

sources.source:
(args) => {
  const {
    changedDisplay,
    unchangedDisplay,
    userLimitUnlimited,
    userLimitValue,
    statePublic,
    statePrivate,
    visibilityStateShown,
    visibilityStateHidden,
    rateLimitedNone,
    rateLimitedDisplay
  } = vars, { newState, oldState } = args;
  return {
    name: newState?.name ?? null,
    nameChanged: newState?.name !== oldState?.name ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    userLimit: newState?.userLimit === 0 ? userLimitUnlimited : userLimitValue,
    userLimitChanged: newState?.userLimit !== oldState?.userLimit ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    userLimitValue: newState?.userLimit ?? 0,
    state: newState?.state === "public" ? statePublic : statePrivate,
    stateChanged: newState?.state !== oldState?.state ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    visibilityState: newState?.visibilityState === "shown" ? visibilityStateShown : visibilityStateHidden,
    visibilityStateChanged: newState?.visibilityState !== oldState?.visibilityState ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    allowedUsers: newState?.allowedUserIds ?? [],
    allowedUsersChanged: JSON.stringify(newState?.allowedUserIds) !== JSON.stringify(oldState?.allowedUserIds) ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    blockedUsers: newState?.blockedUserIds ?? [],
    blockedUsersChanged: JSON.stringify(newState?.blockedUserIds) !== JSON.stringify(oldState?.blockedUserIds) ? changedDisplay : unchangedDisplay,
    rateLimited: args.rateLimitRetryAfter ? rateLimitedDisplay : rateLimitedNone
  };
}

definition.title: 🛡️  Edit Verified Roles Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
Editing verified roles will impact the dynamic channels created by Master Channel #{index}.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide verified roles.

**_Current Verified Roles_**

> {verifiedRolesDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The changes will only affect dynamic channels that change their state after the editing, the old roles in the channel will be be unchanged.

definition.title: 🔑  Edit Staff Roles Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
Staff roles are the mirror of the verified roles: the verified roles are the audience a channel can shut out, the staff roles are the ones it never can.

A role selected here keeps access to every dynamic channel of Master Channel #{index}, whatever privacy state its owner picks - so a moderator can reach a private or hidden channel without being let in one at a time.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide staff roles.

**_Current Staff Roles_**

> {staffRolesDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The changes are applied immediately to the existing dynamic channels.

definition.title: 🎙️  Edit Voice Role Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
A member holds this role only while they sit in a dynamic channel of this master channel, and loses it the moment they leave.

Use it to show a text channel to whoever is in voice right now, or to group them in the member list.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide voice role.

**_Current Voice Role_**

> {voiceRoleDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The bot's own role has to sit above the role it hands out, or discord refuses it.

definition.title: 🔎  Edit LFM Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.footer: Note: The bot needs to view, send messages and embed links in every channel picked here.

definition.title: 🛡️  Edit Default Privacy Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
This is the state a **newly created** dynamic channel starts in. It does not touch channels that already exist, and the owner can still change their own channel afterwards.

**Public** - anyone in the audience can see and join.
**Private** - visible, but only the owner lets people in.
**Hidden** - not visible at all until the owner shows it.

With auto save on, a returning owner gets their own last state instead of this.

**_Current Default_**

> {privacyState}

definition.title: ✋  Edit Default User Limit Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
This is the user limit a **newly created** dynamic channel starts with. It does not touch channels that already exist, and the owner can still change their own channel afterwards.

Copying the generator channel is the old behaviour. Setting a number here is usually better, because the generator's own limit also caps how many people can wait in it at once.

With auto save on, a returning owner gets their own last limit instead of this.

**_Current Default_**

> {userLimitDisplay}

definition.title: Step 1 - Set Dynamic Channels Template Name
definition.description:
You can specify a default name for dynamic channels that will be used when they are opened.

definition.title: Step 3 - Select Verified Roles
definition.description:
Verified roles are the roles that the privacy buttons work on.

When a channel owner presses **Private** or **Hidden**, the bot changes the permissions of these roles. They decide who can see the channel and who can join it.

⚠️ **Not sure what to pick? Keep `@everyone`.** It is the right choice for almost every server.

**_When you need a different role_**

Only if new members cannot see your channels until somebody gives them a role.

_Example_: a new member joins your server and sees nothing until they get the `Member` role. If verified roles stay `@everyone`, a public dynamic channel shows up for that new member too. Pick `Member` instead, and only members who passed your gate can see and join.

**_🛡️ Verified Roles_**

> {verifiedRolesDisplay}

definition.title: 🛡️  Edit Verified Roles Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
Editing verified roles will impact the dynamic channels created by Master Channel #{index}.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide verified roles.

**_Current Verified Roles_**

> {verifiedRolesDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The changes will only affect dynamic channels that change their state after the editing, the old roles in the channel will be be unchanged.

definition.title: 🔑  Edit Staff Roles Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
Staff roles are the mirror of the verified roles: the verified roles are the audience a channel can shut out, the staff roles are the ones it never can.

A role selected here keeps access to every dynamic channel of Master Channel #{index}, whatever privacy state its owner picks - so a moderator can reach a private or hidden channel without being let in one at a time.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide staff roles.

**_Current Staff Roles_**

> {staffRolesDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The changes are applied immediately to the existing dynamic channels.

definition.title: 🎙️  Edit Voice Role Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
A member holds this role only while they sit in a dynamic channel of this master channel, and loses it the moment they leave.

Use it to show a text channel to whoever is in voice right now, or to group them in the member list.

Leaving it empty falls back to the server wide voice role.

**_Current Voice Role_**

> {voiceRoleDisplay}
definition.footer: Note: The bot's own role has to sit above the role it hands out, or discord refuses it.

definition.title: 🛡️  Edit Default Privacy Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
This is the state a **newly created** dynamic channel starts in. It does not touch channels that already exist, and the owner can still change their own channel afterwards.

**Public** - anyone in the audience can see and join.
**Private** - visible, but only the owner lets people in.
**Hidden** - not visible at all until the owner shows it.

With auto save on, a returning owner gets their own last state instead of this.

**_Current Default_**

> {privacyState}

definition.title: ✋  Edit Default User Limit Of Master Channel #{index}
definition.description:
This is the user limit a **newly created** dynamic channel starts with. It does not touch channels that already exist, and the owner can still change their own channel afterwards.

Copying the generator channel is the old behaviour. Setting a number here is usually better, because the generator's own limit also caps how many people can wait in it at once.

With auto save on, a returning owner gets their own last limit instead of this.

**_Current Default_**

> {userLimitDisplay}
